hero.headline: Senate Intelligence Chair calls Trump intelligence pick a national security risk
hero.body:
Senate Intelligence Committee Chair Mark Warner described Bill Pulte, named by President Trump as acting director of national intelligence, as a national security risk. Warner made the statement as scrutiny intensifies over Pulte's appointment to oversee the nation's intelligence agencies.

Representative Jim Himes joined the criticism, calling Pulte in an intelligence role Trump's worst and most dangerous appointment. The concerns from senior lawmakers on intelligence matters highlight opposition to Pulte's qualifications for the position. Trump has stated he wants Pulte to reduce the size of the Office of the Director of National Intelligence.

The position of director of national intelligence oversees 18 intelligence agencies including the CIA and NSA. The role was created after the September 11 attacks to coordinate intelligence gathering and sharing across the government. Pulte's appointment comes as Trump moves to reshape the intelligence community.

Separately, uncertainty has emerged around the Trump administration's plan to spin off mortgage giants Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac. The two government-sponsored enterprises have been under federal conservatorship since the 2008 financial crisis. Any restructuring would have significant implications for the housing finance system and mortgage markets.

The intelligence appointment requires Senate confirmation, where Warner's committee will play a central role in evaluating Pulte's background and qualifications. The public criticism from the committee chair signals potential difficulty in securing confirmation votes. Trump has made overhauling intelligence agencies a priority, arguing they need restructuring and size reduction.

cards.headline: US launches airstrikes on Iranian sites after Iran fires drones
cards.teaser: The US conducted retaliatory strikes after Iran launched missiles and drones in attacks over the weekend.
cards.body:
The United States carried out airstrikes on Iranian sites after Iran launched missiles and drones in weekend attacks, according to military reports. The exchange of fire tests a fragile ceasefire between the two nations and represents the latest flare-up in ongoing tensions in the Gulf region.

Iran accused the US of violating the ceasefire following the American strikes. Iranian officials said contradictory positions from the US remain the main issue blocking progress in ongoing negotiations. The new round of military action comes as both sides have been engaged in stalled peace talks, with neither making significant progress toward a lasting agreement.

cards.headline: Israel strikes Beirut suburbs days after US-brokered ceasefire
cards.body:
Israel launched airstrikes on Beirut's southern suburbs on Sunday, escalating tensions just days after a ceasefire proposal was announced. The Israeli military said the strikes targeted "terrorist headquarters" in response to Hezbollah firing at Israeli territory. The attacks killed two people and wounded 11, according to Lebanon's state news agency.

The strikes hit two apartments in separate buildings, covering streets with rubble and triggering evacuations from the southern suburbs. Israeli media reported that the US had been informed before the operation, though Washington had previously asked Israel not to strike Beirut itself.

The renewed violence marks a significant breakdown of diplomatic efforts. Lebanon's government and Israel had agreed to a ceasefire proposal that was being negotiated in Washington, but Hezbollah rejected the terms. The militant group has stated it will not accept any ceasefire that does not include Israeli troop withdrawal from Lebanon and an end to Israeli strikes across the country.

Israeli officials said they had intercepted Hezbollah rocket fire on Sunday morning, though Hezbollah did not claim responsibility for those attacks. The strikes represent the most serious escalation since a ceasefire was established in mid-April.

The escalation has prompted a strong response from Iran. Ebrahim Rezaei, spokesperson for parliament's foreign policy committee, said on social media that Iran would deliver "a decisive and painful response" to the strikes. He wrote: "We will give a decisive and painful response to the Zionist regime's attack on the suburbs. Watch the sky of the occupied territories tonight." Iran had previously warned that any Israeli attack on Beirut would be considered a violation of a US-Iran ceasefire and would trigger Iranian retaliation.

Israeli media reported expectations of a limited attack from Iran and Hezbollah in response to Sunday's strike. The situation has revived concerns about broader regional conflict after tensions had appeared to ease following the April ceasefire.

The fighting in Lebanon began on March 2 when Hezbollah launched rockets at Israel following the killing of Iran's supreme leader. Israeli strikes have killed more than 3,613 people in Lebanon, while Hezbollah has killed at least 30 Israeli soldiers and 3 Israeli civilians.

The conflict has complicated broader Middle East peace negotiations. Iran has insisted that Lebanon be included in any comprehensive ceasefire agreement with the US, while US officials have indicated they are not making Lebanon a requirement for an Iran deal.

The uncertainty around negotiations in Washington and the renewed strikes raise questions about the viability of further diplomatic breakthroughs. Hezbollah's rejection of the ceasefire proposal and Israel's decision to strike Beirut suggest that the parties remain far apart on fundamental terms for ending the conflict.

cards.headline: Russian drone strikes spent nuclear fuel storage near Chornobyl
cards.teaser: Ukrainian officials say a Russian drone hit a storage facility for spent nuclear fuel near the Chornobyl nuclear plant.
cards.body:
A Russian Shahed drone substantially damaged a building at a spent nuclear fuel storage facility near the disused Chornobyl nuclear power plant. Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky condemned the attack as deliberate and "extremely vile," calling attention to the dangers of targeting sensitive nuclear sites.

The reception building of the storage facility was empty of fuel containers at the time of the strike. The attack appeared designed as a direct message from Moscow amid intensifying aerial warfare, with both sides targeting high-profile locations.

cards.headline: Ukraine seeks European mediators as US steps back from peace talks
cards.teaser: President Volodymyr Zelensky traveled to London to meet with leaders of Britain, Germany and France as potential negotiators with Russia.
cards.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky traveled to London to meet with the leaders of Britain, Germany and France. He proposed that these European leaders could serve as negotiators in potential peace talks with Russia, marking a shift in Ukraine's diplomatic strategy away from US-led mediation efforts.

The meeting brought together key Western allies to discuss pathways forward for negotiations as the conflict continues without resolution in sight.

cards.headline: OPEC+ Approves Fourth Oil Output Increase Since Strait of Hormuz Closure
cards.body:
OPEC and its allies approved a fourth oil production quota increase for July, adding 188,000 barrels per day to their output targets. The decision comes as the ongoing conflict in the Middle East continues to block oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz, a critical waterway for global energy supplies.

The production increase is largely symbolic given that vast amounts of the world's oil remain stranded due to the effective shutdown of the strait. Despite the higher quotas, actual oil exports remain severely constrained by the closure, which has disrupted the flow of crude from major producers in the Persian Gulf region.

The cartel's move to boost output targets reflects an attempt to signal supply availability even as the physical infrastructure for delivering that oil remains compromised. The Strait of Hormuz normally handles about one-fifth of global oil consumption, making its closure a significant constraint on world energy markets regardless of production levels.

The decision was made by delegates from OPEC member countries and allied producers during their latest meeting. The group has now approved four separate quota increases since the strait's closure, each representing efforts to manage supply expectations amid the ongoing regional conflict.

The situation underscores the complex relationship between oil production capacity and actual delivery capability. While producers can increase output at their facilities, the inability to transport crude through normal shipping channels limits the practical impact of higher production quotas on global supply.

cards.headline: Iranians face economic despair amid war casualties and soaring inflation
cards.teaser: An imploding economy is causing widespread hopelessness among both supporters and opponents of the Iranian government.
cards.body:
Iranians are experiencing severe economic hardship as the country faces both war deaths and skyrocketing inflation. The economic crisis has created despair among citizens across the political spectrum, affecting both those who support and oppose the government.

For Iranians who had hoped for regime change, the current situation has brought particular disappointment. The imploding economy has worsened living conditions nationwide, with inflation eroding purchasing power and making basic goods increasingly unaffordable. The dual pressures of conflict casualties and economic collapse have deepened the sense of hopelessness throughout the country.

cards.teaser: President Volodymyr Zelensky traveled to London to meet with leaders of Britain, Germany and France as potential negotiators with Russia.

He proposed that these European leaders could serve as negotiators in potential peace talks with Russia, marking a shift in Ukraine's diplomatic strategy away from US-led mediation efforts.

cards.headline: Peru holds presidential runoff election
cards.teaser: Voters in Peru are deciding between candidates in a tight presidential race seen as a test of Latin America's rightward political shift.
cards.body:
Peru held a presidential runoff election pitting Keiko Fujimori, a right-wing candidate and daughter of former president Alberto Fujimori, against Roberto Sánchez, a leftist congressman and former trade and tourism minister. Fujimori had won 17 percent in the first round, while Sánchez secured 12 percent, advancing past ultra-conservative Rafael López Aliaga.

The election reflected Peru's political polarization and came amid widespread voter frustration over rising crime, corruption and instability. Peru has had nine presidents in a decade, leaving many voters seeking stability and leadership focused on tackling inequality. The runoff represented a straight left-right ideological choice for Peruvian voters.

cards.headline: Nigerian military frees hundreds held by Boko Haram
cards.teaser: Hundreds of captives, including many women and children, were freed from a Boko Haram mountain hideout.
cards.body:
Nigerian forces have liberated hundreds of people from a Boko Haram stronghold in a mountain area near the Cameroon border. Among those freed were many women and children who had been held captive since their abduction in March.

The rescue operation targeted the remote militant hideout where Boko Haram had been keeping the prisoners. The group has a long history of kidnappings across northeastern Nigeria and surrounding regions, using abductions for ransom and forced recruitment into its ranks.

cards.headline: Former Oregon Senator Bob Packwood dies at 93
cards.teaser: Bob Packwood, who resigned from the Senate following sexual misconduct allegations, has died at age 93.
cards.body:
Bob Packwood, a former senator from Oregon who was forced to resign in the 1990s following a sexual misconduct scandal, died at 93. Packwood served in the Senate for nearly three decades before his resignation.

Packwood left office after a Senate Ethics Committee investigation into allegations of sexual harassment and misconduct. His departure marked one of the most prominent congressional ethics cases of that era. He had been in hospice care before his death.

cards.headline: Trump ends interview with Meet the Press host
cards.teaser: President Trump cut short an interview with NBC's Kristen Welker, telling her he had enough.
cards.body:
President Trump ended an interview with Meet the Press host Kristen Welker before its scheduled conclusion. Trump told Welker he had had enough and walked away from the sit-down.

The interview took place outdoors in rainy conditions and grew contentious between Trump and the NBC News journalist. The exchange covered multiple topics before Trump terminated the conversation. NBC News conducted fact-checking of statements made during the interview.

cards.headline: South Carolina governor's race tests Trump endorsement power
cards.teaser: The South Carolina governor's race has become a test case for the strength of a Trump endorsement.
cards.body:
The South Carolina gubernatorial race is emerging as a key test of President Trump's political influence. Representative Nancy Mace is competing in the race despite complications in her relationship with Trump following her vote on legislation related to the Epstein files.

Mace has downplayed concerns about the political consequences of her vote, suggesting that Trump's endorsement alone will not determine the outcome. She has characterized the race as highly competitive, indicating that multiple factors beyond Trump's support will shape the final result.

cards.headline: Israel strikes Beirut suburb after US-brokered ceasefire
cards.teaser: Israel attacked a Beirut suburb days after a US-brokered truce, citing Hezbollah fire into Israeli territory.
cards.body:
Israel conducted strikes on a Beirut suburb days after a US-brokered ceasefire between Israel and Hezbollah took effect. Israeli officials said the attacks were ordered in response to Hezbollah firing at Israeli territory.

The renewed military action raises concerns about the stability of the truce. Hezbollah and Israel have been engaged in cross-border hostilities for months.

cards.headline: Zelensky condemns Russian drone strike near Chornobyl nuclear plant
cards.teaser: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky criticized a Russian drone strike on a facility near the Chornobyl nuclear plant.
cards.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky condemned a Russian drone attack on the Chornobyl nuclear facility, calling it "extremely vile" and deliberate. A Shahed drone struck a reception building at the spent nuclear fuel storage facility near the disused power plant.

Though the building was empty of fuel containers at the time of the strike, the attack appeared to be a direct message from Moscow as both sides intensify long-range aerial bombardments. Zelensky made his remarks while preparing for talks in London, with the Chornobyl site remaining a persistent concern throughout the conflict due to potential radiological risks.

cards.headline: US and Iran remain far from peace deal 100 days into war
cards.teaser: Peace negotiations between the United States and Iran have stalled as the conflict reaches the 100-day mark.
cards.body:
The United States and Iran appear far from reaching a peace agreement as their military conflict enters its 100th day. Peace talks between the two nations have reached a stalemate with no clear path forward.

Multiple news outlets described the negotiations as deadlocked. The extended duration of hostilities has raised concerns about regional stability and the prospects for a diplomatic resolution. Both sides have continued military operations while talks remain at an impasse.

cards.headline: Trump Criticizes Potential Federal Reserve Interest Rate Increases
cards.teaser: The president said raising interest rates would be wrong, speaking ahead of the debut of the new Federal Reserve chair.
cards.body:
President Trump said the Federal Reserve should not raise interest rates and called for cuts instead. His comments came ahead of Kevin Warsh's debut as incoming Fed Chair.

Trump stated there was no reason to raise rates following the latest jobs report. While he said the Fed chair should do whatever he wants, he made clear his preference for lower rates rather than increases. The president has consistently advocated for lower interest rates throughout his term.

cards.headline: Banks Prepare for Workforce Reductions as Artificial Intelligence Adoption Expands
cards.teaser: Financial institutions are laying groundwork for significant job cuts as AI technology becomes more integrated into banking operations.
cards.body:
Major banks are establishing the foundation for large-scale workforce reductions as artificial intelligence takes hold across the industry. The preparations signal a shift in how financial institutions plan to deploy technology in place of human workers.

The moves come as AI capabilities expand in banking operations, from customer service to back-office functions. Banks are positioning themselves to reduce headcount as automated systems handle tasks previously performed by employees.

cards.headline: Eli Lilly Reports Triple-Action Diabetes Drug Reduces Blood Sugar and Weight
cards.teaser: The pharmaceutical company's next-generation obesity medication showed improvements across multiple health metrics in clinical trials.
cards.body:
Phase 3 trial results show that retatrutide, a weekly injection for type 2 diabetes, significantly outperformed placebo across multiple measures. Patients receiving the drug for 40 weeks lost more than four times as much weight as those on placebo, while their long-term blood sugar levels dropped more than twice as much.

Retatrutide works by mimicking three gut hormones—GLP-1, GIP, and glucagon—that regulate appetite, blood sugar, and metabolism. This triple mechanism distinguishes it from existing treatments like Ozempic and Mounjaro, which target fewer pathways. The glucagon component specifically boosts the body's energy expenditure, offering a more comprehensive approach to managing type 2 diabetes and weight control.

cards.headline: Italian Banks Pursue Merger Talks as Intesa Prepares Counterbid
cards.teaser: Banco BPM proposed a merger with Monte dei Paschi as Intesa Sanpaolo prepares to enter the competition for the Italian lender.
cards.body:
Banco BPM has invited Monte dei Paschi to merge in a deal that would create Italy's second-largest bank. The proposed combination is valued at approximately €50 billion and is being structured as a merger of equals between the two Italian lenders.

Intesa Sanpaolo is preparing a competing bid for Monte dei Paschi that could derail the BPM merger talks. The move reflects intensifying consolidation activity in Italy's banking sector, with other institutions like BPER also considering potential strategic moves.

cards.headline: Marks and Spencer Launches Training Program for 1,000 Young People
cards.teaser: The British retailer introduced a new traineeship scheme aimed at young people not currently in employment, education, or training.
cards.body:
Marks and Spencer has launched a new traineeship program aimed at 1,000 young people who are not currently in employment, education, or training. The initiative directly addresses what the company identifies as a growing challenge facing this demographic.

The scheme represents M&S's effort to support young people in overcoming barriers to entering the workforce and engaging with traditional career pathways.

cards.headline: Tata Steel Warns of Possible Delay for New Furnace Over Electrical Issue
cards.teaser: The company said its 1.25 billion pound steel-making furnace project may face delays due to an electrical connectivity problem.
cards.body:
Tata Steel has flagged a potential delay to its £1.25 billion steel-making furnace project due to an electrical connectivity issue. The problem has emerged during construction of the new facility.

The electrical challenge represents a technical hurdle that could push back the timeline for the furnace to become operational. Tata Steel has identified this connectivity issue as the main factor that may affect when the project comes online.

hero.headline: Bumblebees solve complex problems without training, study finds
hero.body:
Bumblebees have demonstrated the ability to spontaneously solve problems previously thought to require the large brains of animals like chimpanzees and elephants. New research published in the journal Science shows that these insects can use tools to complete tasks they have never encountered before, challenging assumptions about the relationship between brain size and intelligence.

Researchers at the University of Oulu in Finland conducted experiments based on a classic test from a century ago. In that original study, chimpanzees solved the "box-and-banana" problem by stacking boxes to reach food. Since then, various primates, elephants, and crows have demonstrated similar problem-solving abilities. Now bumblebees have joined this exclusive group.

In the experiment, bees were first trained to associate a blue artificial flower with a sugar water reward. The flower was then moved to the ceiling of a chamber too high for the bees to reach by flying. A polystyrene ball was placed in the chamber. To access the flower, the bees had to roll the ball beneath it and climb on top, a sequence they had never performed or been trained to do. In the basic version of the test, 75 percent of the bees succeeded.

To determine whether the bees were truly solving the problem or simply getting lucky, researchers created increasingly difficult versions of the challenge. In the final test, bees explored two chambers, only one containing the artificial flower. Scientists then filled the chamber with red light, preventing the bees from seeing the blue flower, and introduced the ball. The bees had to remember the flower's location and position the ball correctly. Twenty-three out of thirty bees succeeded.

Dr. Olli Loukola, the senior researcher, emphasized that the findings challenge common misconceptions about insects. "Most people think insects are reflex-based machines," he said. "That they can't have any emotional states or feel pain. Some people don't even realize that they have brains. I hope that these results change the worldview about that."

The research demonstrates that complex problem-solving does not require the neural architecture of mammals and birds. Instead, insects with fewer than one million neurons can generate flexible solutions to novel problems through efficient brain organization.

Professor Lars Chittka from Queen Mary University of London, who was not involved in the study, called the findings "the clearest demonstration yet of some kind of comprehension of what's at stake." He noted that the results challenge the assumption that intelligent behavior requires big brains. "Bees are a model of how much intelligence you can squeeze into a small nervous system," Chittka said. "It's a good reminder of there being a motivation to pay some respect to these other beings."

The findings have implications for understanding how intelligence evolved and could inform the development of compact artificial intelligence systems that perform sophisticated tasks without massive computing resources.

cards.headline: School shooting survivor sues AI gun detection company after system failed to spot weapon
cards.teaser: A survivor of a school shooting filed a lawsuit against an artificial intelligence gun detection firm after the system failed to identify a weapon before an attack.
cards.body:
The lawsuit raises questions about the accuracy standards required for AI security systems deployed in schools and public spaces. The gun detection system was installed at the school where the shooting occurred, but failed to alert staff to the presence of a firearm before the incident.

The case puts AI security companies under scrutiny as schools increasingly rely on automated detection systems to prevent violence. The legal action could establish precedents for liability when AI safety systems fail to perform as advertised, particularly in life-or-death situations where human safety depends on technology accuracy.

cards.headline: Nvidia and Microsoft unveil new PC chips for personal AI applications
cards.teaser: Nvidia introduced new PC processors designed to run AI applications locally, partnering with Microsoft on devices including the Surface Laptop Ultra showcased at Computex.
cards.body:
The chips represent Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's strategy to compete across all levels of the AI technology stack, moving into territory traditionally held by Intel and Qualcomm. Microsoft demonstrated the Surface Laptop Ultra and Surface Dev Box equipped with the new processors at the Computex trade show.

The announcement signals a shift toward AI processing happening directly on personal computers rather than in cloud data centers. Analysts identified Intel and Qualcomm as potential losers in the competitive landscape as Nvidia expands beyond its traditional graphics and data center markets into consumer PC processors.

cards.headline: Virtual OS Museum launches with over 600 operating systems available on desktop
cards.teaser: A new online archive allows users to run more than 600 historical operating systems directly from their desktop computers.
cards.body:
The Virtual OS Museum is a collection of over 1,700 distinct installations spanning more than 600 operating systems across 250+ platforms. Users can download and run these systems via emulation directly on their computers, allowing them to experience legacy computing environments without needing original hardware.

The project is primarily the work of Andrew Warkentin, a developer and OS historian who has been assembling the collection over time. The museum serves as a digital archive of computing history, preserving operating systems that would otherwise become inaccessible as physical media deteriorates and compatible hardware disappears.

cards.headline: Researchers identify ancient Chinese medicine compound as potential hair loss treatment
cards.teaser: Scientists studying traditional Chinese medicine identified a compound that could offer a new approach to treating hair loss.
cards.body:
The research examined substances used in ancient Chinese medicinal practices and isolated a specific compound showing promise for hair regrowth. The findings were published in a peer-reviewed scientific journal.

The discovery could lead to new pharmaceutical treatments for baldness and hair thinning conditions. Researchers are investigating how the compound affects hair follicles and whether it can be developed into a viable therapeutic option for patients experiencing hair loss.

cards.headline: Report details major security breaches and data leaks in first half of 2026
cards.teaser: A review of 2026 security incidents documented multiple significant data breaches including compromised government systems and critical infrastructure attacks.
cards.body:
The first six months of 2026 saw several significant cyber incidents, including a breach of a government department, compromises to energy and water infrastructure systems, and an attack on an FBI surveillance system. These breaches resulted in stolen data and ransom demands, exposing vulnerabilities in critical systems that protect both government operations and essential services.

Cybersecurity experts compiled a review assessing the severity and frequency of attacks during this period. The incidents highlighted weaknesses in how sensitive data and infrastructure are currently protected, prompting questions about whether existing security measures are adequate for safeguarding these vital systems.

cards.headline: Xbox Games Showcase 2026 features announcements under new CEO Asha Sharma
cards.teaser: Microsoft held its annual Xbox Games Showcase with new CEO Asha Sharma presenting for the first time, unveiling upcoming titles and platform updates.
cards.body:
Microsoft held its Xbox Games Showcase on June 7th at Summer Game Fest, where newly appointed CEO Asha Sharma made her debut presentation at the company's flagship gaming event. The showcase featured trailers and announcements for upcoming Xbox titles.

The event showcased Microsoft's gaming strategy and upcoming release calendar. Like PlayStation's recent showcase focusing on single-player experiences, Xbox used the platform to present its gaming direction to the industry.

hero.headline: Mercedes driver Antonelli wins fifth consecutive F1 race at Monaco
hero.teaser: Kimi Antonelli extended his winning streak with a dominant performance at the Monaco Grand Prix despite a late red flag.
hero.body:
Kimi Antonelli claimed his fifth consecutive Formula 1 victory at the Monaco Grand Prix on Sunday, delivering a dominant performance from pole position despite dramatic circumstances in the closing stages of the race.

The 19-year-old Mercedes driver became the youngest winner ever at Monaco, controlling the race throughout until two safety car periods and a red flag created late-race chaos. Antonelli managed the pressure expertly during two restarts, holding off Lewis Hamilton who finished second, with Red Bull's Isack Hadjar completing the podium in third.

The red flag was triggered when the track surface began breaking up at the final corner, requiring a complete standing restart. Despite the pressure of multiple restarts, Antonelli maintained his composure to secure the victory.

This winning streak represents one of the most impressive performances in recent F1 history. The Italian's success this season has drawn comparisons to other elite young performers in sport. Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff has praised Antonelli's rapid development, noting that his ability to capitalize on the team's competitive car every weekend has exceeded expectations.

Antonelli's third consecutive victory came at Miami, where he defeated Lando Norris's McLaren in a tight battle. That performance prompted Wolff to describe it as his best race yet. The teenager has shown remarkable improvement from his debut season, moving away from the unforced errors and excessive aggression that occasionally marked his rookie campaign.

"It's astounding what he's doing these past few races," Wolff said. "We predicted ups and downs in his first year, moments of brilliance mixed with moments of frustration. This year it's all coming together in a way none of us fully anticipated."

The Mercedes team principal credited Antonelli's family with keeping him grounded despite the mounting pressure and attention. The driver's success has made him and tennis star Jannik Sinner dominant figures in Italian sports, with both recording major victories on the same weekends multiple times this season.

Antonelli currently leads the world championship by twenty points over his Mercedes teammate George Russell, just two seasons into his F1 career. His emergence as a title contender represents a significant achievement given the competitive nature of modern Formula 1.

The victory continues Mercedes' unbeaten record in grand prix races this season, following George Russell's win at the season opener in Australia. However, it is Antonelli's rapid adaptation to the pressure of leading the championship that has most impressed those within the sport, as the teenager demonstrates the composure and consistency required to compete at the highest level.

cards.headline: Golden Tempo wins Belmont Stakes to complete partial Triple Crown
cards.teaser: The Kentucky Derby winner captured the third leg of the Triple Crown five weeks after his Derby victory.
cards.body:
Golden Tempo won the Belmont Stakes on Saturday, capturing the third leg of the Triple Crown five weeks after winning the Kentucky Derby. The victory adds another accomplishment for trainer Cherie DeVaux, who continues to make history in thoroughbred racing.

By winning both the Derby and the Belmont, Golden Tempo and DeVaux have joined a select group of trainers to achieve this milestone in the sport.

cards.headline: Golden Knights rally from four-goal deficit to take 2-1 Stanley Cup Final lead
cards.teaser: The Vegas Golden Knights recovered from blowing a four-goal lead to defeat the Carolina Hurricanes 5-4 in double overtime in Game 3 of the Stanley Cup Final on .
cards.body:
The Vegas Golden Knights defeated the Carolina Hurricanes 5-4 in double overtime in Game 3 of the Stanley Cup Final on Saturday, securing a 2-1 series lead. Defenseman Shea Theodore scored the winning goal at 5:38 of the second overtime period, with the puck deflecting off goalie Brandon Bussi's skate.

Vegas built an early four-goal lead before Carolina mounted an impressive comeback, scoring four straight goals to force overtime. Mitch Marner recorded the fastest hat trick in Stanley Cup Final history during the game. The Golden Knights now need two more wins to claim their second Stanley Cup championship.

cards.headline: Brewers pitcher sets record with 103.7 mph fastball
cards.teaser: Jacob Misiorowski threw the fastest pitch by a starting pitcher since tracking began in 2008.
cards.body:
Milwaukee Brewers pitcher Jacob Misiorowski threw a 103.7 mph fastball during Saturday's game against the Colorado Rockies, breaking the record for the fastest pitch by a starting pitcher since MLB began tracking velocity in 2008.

The achievement highlights Misiorowski's exceptional arm strength among starting pitchers in the league.

cards.headline: Welterweight Bonfim dominates former champion Muhammad at UFC Fight Night
cards.teaser: Gabriel Bonfim improved to 20-1 with a breakout performance against Belal Muhammad in Las Vegas.
cards.body:
Welterweight Gabriel Bonfim delivered a breakout performance Saturday night at UFC Fight Night in Las Vegas, dominating former champion Belal Muhammad. Bonfim improved to 20-1 with the victory, while Muhammad fell to 24-6.

Throughout the fight, Bonfim controlled the action and frequently smiled and laughed during exchanges with his opponent. The dominant showing represents a significant breakthrough for the Brazilian fighter as he moves toward title contention in the welterweight division.

cards.headline: Mystics coach ejected and escorted by police after arguing with officials
cards.teaser: Sydney Johnson had to be held back during a heated exchange with referees in a blowout loss to Atlanta.
cards.body:
Washington Mystics coach Sydney Johnson was ejected from Saturday's game against the Atlanta Dream after a heated argument with officials. Johnson had to be physically restrained while disputing calls during the blowout loss to the host Dream.

Following his ejection, Johnson was escorted off the court by police. The incident marked an unusual scene as law enforcement became involved in removing the coach from the playing area.

cards.headline: Several fans injured as storm damages tent at West Virginia baseball game
cards.teaser: Heavy winds knocked over an event tent next to the ballpark during a super regional game on Saturday.
cards.body:
At least five fans were injured Saturday when heavy winds knocked over an event tent next to Kendrick Family Ballpark during West Virginia's super regional baseball game. The storm struck during the NCAA tournament contest, creating an emergency situation at the venue.

The university confirmed the incident and the injuries sustained by attendees, though specific details about the nature and severity of the injuries were not provided.

hero.headline: Scott Pelley Speaks Out After 60 Minutes Firing, Calls for Removal of Bari Weiss
hero.body:
Scott Pelley, a veteran CBS News journalist who spent decades at 60 Minutes, was fired by the network after publicly criticizing editor-in-chief Bari Weiss during a heated staff meeting. Pelley has since accused the network's new leadership of interfering with reporting and pushing him to compromise journalistic integrity.

The conflict erupted following a wave of layoffs at 60 Minutes that removed the show's executive producer, executive editor, and two correspondents including Cecilia Vega and Sharyn Alfonsi. During a Monday morning meeting with newly appointed executive editor Nick Bilton and other CBS News executives, Pelley directly attacked Weiss's leadership. "She's murdering 60 Minutes," Pelley said. "She does not love this place. She was brought in to kill it and is doing exactly that."

After the meeting, Weiss informed Pelley that his behavior was inappropriate. He was terminated the following day, with Bilton citing Pelley's "incivility and contempt" in the dismissal message. Bilton wrote that Pelley had "hijacked" the staff meeting to disparage him and his qualifications.

Pelley has not remained silent since his termination. He issued a public statement accusing CBS News executives of silencing employees and instructing him "to inject falsehoods and bias" into his reporting. He emphasized that 60 Minutes has maintained its position as America's top-rated program because audiences trust its integrity and quality.

Pelley has also claimed that management interfered with a segment examining an immigration officer's killing of Minneapolis protester Renee Good. According to Pelley, Weiss requested changes to the broadcast, allegedly because the reporting echoed statements made by President Trump.

Pelley's firing marks a significant moment at the storied news program, which is facing major changes. Anderson Cooper announced his departure earlier this year, leaving 60 Minutes with only three full-time correspondents as it enters its 59th season: Lesley Stahl, Bill Whitaker, and Jon Wertheim. Norah O'Donnell also contributes to the program.

The situation has drawn commentary from prominent figures connected to 60 Minutes' history. Sarah Safer, daughter of legendary 60 Minutes correspondent Morley Safer, expressed outrage at the current direction of the program. Rome Hartman, a longtime 60 Minutes producer, called Pelley "among the all-time greats" and noted the irony that Weiss's organization, the Free Press, positions itself against cancel culture while terminating someone for pushing back during a staff meeting.

Pelley joined CBS News in 1989 and served as chief White House correspondent and anchor of the CBS Evening News before becoming a 60 Minutes correspondent. His departure represents a major loss for the program as it navigates leadership changes under new parent company ownership.

cards.headline: Scary Movie Opens With $55 Million, Best Franchise Start
cards.teaser: The rebooted horror parody led the weekend box office with a franchise-record opening.
cards.body:
Paramount's Scary Movie claimed the weekend box office with a franchise-record $55 million opening. The spoof comedy arrived during an unusual summer surge for horror films, alongside fellow genre entries Backrooms and Obsession, which also performed strongly at the North American box office.

Masters of the Universe disappointed in its debut, earning $29.3 million and falling below industry expectations. The unexpected dominance of three horror titles at the top of the charts marked a notable shift from typical summer blockbuster patterns, with the genre claiming the weekend's strongest positions.

cards.headline: Super Mario Galaxy Movie Crosses $1 Billion, First 2026 Film to Hit Milestone
cards.teaser: The animated video game adaptation became the year's first billion-dollar box office hit.
cards.body:
The Super Mario Galaxy Movie has become the first film released in 2026 to cross $1 billion at the global box office. The animated feature was produced by Universal and Illumination in partnership with Nintendo, with a production budget of $110 million.

The milestone underscores the continued strength of video game adaptations in theatrical releases. The Super Mario franchise has demonstrated particular appeal across audiences, drawing both longtime fans and general moviegoers to cinemas.

cards.headline: Iranian Court Upholds One-Year Prison Sentence for Filmmaker Jafar Panahi
cards.teaser: A Tehran court rejected the Palme d'Or winner's appeal of his conviction on propaganda charges.
cards.body:
Tehran's Revolutionary Court upheld a one-year prison sentence against filmmaker Jafar Panahi, who won the Palme d'Or at the Cannes Film Festival. Panahi had been sentenced in December in absentia on charges of engaging in propaganda activities against the Iranian state. His lawyer Mostafa Nili announced the decision to reject the director's appeal during a press briefing in Tehran.

Panahi's case reflects ongoing tensions between Iranian authorities and artists who have been critical of the government. The filmmaker has faced restrictions and legal challenges related to his work for years, with authorities citing his films as problematic under Iranian law.

cards.headline: Interview With the Vampire Transforms Into The Vampire Lestat for Season 3
cards.teaser: The AMC series shifts focus to a new title character in its third season.
cards.body:
AMC's Interview With the Vampire undergoes what creator and showrunner Rolin Jones calls the Great Transformation in its third season. The phrase carries meaning within Anne Rice's world of vampires and spell-casters, but also serves as a description of the show's own evolution. Characters throughout the season speak of this transformation with a mix of dread, anticipation, and awe.

The series adapts Rice's novels with a focus on Lestat as the central figure for the new season. Jones's interpretation continues to build on the lush and theatrical world established in the show's first two seasons, drawing from Rice's extensive mythology of supernatural beings.

cards.headline: Federal Lawsuit Against Kennedy Center Jazz Musician Dismissed
cards.teaser: A judge withdrew the Trump administration's breach of contract case against Chuck Redd.
cards.body:
A judge dismissed a $1 million breach of contract lawsuit filed by the Trump administration against Kennedy Center Christmas jazz musician Chuck Redd. The lawsuit was withdrawn based on Washington, D.C.'s anti-SLAPP protections, which shield defendants from legal actions intended to silence speech or public participation.

The case involved claims related to Redd's performance at the Kennedy Center. The dismissal represents a legal victory for the musician under D.C. statutes designed to prevent strategic lawsuits from suppressing protected expression.

cards.headline: Disney Executive Naomi Bulochnikov-Paul Honored at Race to Erase MS Gala
cards.teaser: The senior Disney executive spoke about her journey living with multiple sclerosis.
cards.body:
Disney executive Naomi Bulochnikov-Paul received recognition at the annual Race to Erase MS gala, where she discussed her experience with multiple sclerosis. Speaking from the heart, Bulochnikov-Paul described the surprise of receiving her diagnosis and how she has approached living with the condition. The senior executive said she lives with MS openly.

As a senior executive at Disney, Bulochnikov-Paul has balanced her professional responsibilities with managing her health condition. The Race to Erase MS gala brings together supporters and advocates working to fund research and support for people living with multiple sclerosis.

hero.headline: Deb Haaland wins New Mexico Democratic primary for governor
hero.teaser: The former Biden administration official could become the first female Native American governor if elected.
hero.body:
Former Interior Secretary Deb Haaland won the Democratic primary for governor of New Mexico. Haaland served in President Biden's cabinet before launching her gubernatorial campaign.

If successful in the general election, Haaland would make history as the first female Native American governor in the United States. She previously represented New Mexico in Congress before joining the Biden administration.

cards.headline: Trump defends anti-weaponization fund despite DOJ decision to halt it
cards.teaser: The president said the controversial fund was a great idea, even after the acting attorney general said it would not move forward.
cards.body:
President Trump defended his administration's "anti-weaponization" fund during a Sunday NBC News interview, despite acting Attorney General Todd Blanche's announcement that the Department of Justice would not proceed with the program. Trump called the fund "a great idea" and expressed support for compensating individuals he believes were treated unfairly by prosecutors.

When asked whether the fund could be used for Capitol rioters charged with assaulting police officers on January 6, 2021, Trump declined to rule it out. He argued that those who entered the Capitol had been treated unfairly and suggested they deserved compensation, saying "I'd pay the kind of money they deserve."

cards.headline: Trump abruptly ends NBC interview after questions on California primary claims
cards.teaser: President Trump cut short a lengthy interview with NBC News host Kristen Welker on Friday after she pressed him on his claim that the California gubernatorial p.
cards.body:
President Trump cut short a lengthy interview with NBC News host Kristen Welker on Friday after she pressed him on his claim that the California gubernatorial primary was rigged. The interview, conducted in Wisconsin and aired Sunday on Meet the Press, ended when Trump told Welker he had had enough.

During the exchange, Trump repeated his assertion that the 2020 presidential election was rigged, a claim that has been repeatedly rejected by courts and election officials across the country. When Welker questioned his similar statements about the ongoing California gubernatorial primary, the president ended the interview.

The abrupt conclusion came as California voters were deciding between several Democratic candidates including Katie Porter, Tom Steyer, and Xavier Becerra, and Republicans Chad Bianco and Steve Hilton in the race to replace Governor Gavin Newsom. Trump has provided no evidence to support his claims about irregularities in the California contest.

The interview covered other topics before its early end. Trump defended his administration's anti-weaponization fund, which acting Attorney General Todd Blanche said would not move forward. Trump told Welker he thought the fund was a great idea and said many other Republicans agreed with him. The fund was intended to compensate people who claimed they were wronged by government investigations.

The president's willingness to end interviews when faced with challenging questions has become a pattern during his administration. The exchange with Welker highlighted ongoing tensions between the White House and mainstream news organizations over coverage of Trump's statements about election integrity and other controversial topics.

cards.headline: Hilton and Becerra lead in California governor primary
cards.teaser: Results are coming in as Democrats and Republicans compete for nominations to replace Governor Gavin Newsom.
cards.body:
Republican Steve Hilton and Democrat Xavier Becerra are leading their respective parties in California's gubernatorial primary. The race includes Democrats Katie Porter and Tom Steyer, along with Republican Chad Bianco, all competing for the chance to succeed Governor Gavin Newsom.

The primary will determine which candidates advance to the general election for one of the most prominent state executive offices in the country. California governors often play significant roles in national policy debates on issues ranging from climate change to immigration.

cards.headline: Senator Warner says Democrats have been too bureaucratic
cards.teaser: The Virginia Democrat called for his party to focus on growth and innovation amid polling struggles.
cards.body:
Senator Mark Warner of Virginia criticized the Democratic Party for being excessively bureaucratic as the party continues to face low approval ratings. Warner said Democrats need to articulate a fuller strategy beyond simply opposing President Trump.

The senator called for the Democratic Party to become pro-growth and pro-innovation. His comments reflect broader concerns within the party about how to rebuild public support and develop a compelling economic message for voters.

cards.headline: DOJ has alternative pathways for payouts after anti-weaponization fund halted
cards.teaser: Officials and lawmakers are exploring other routes to compensate those claiming government wrongdoing.
cards.body:
I need to flag a significant discrepancy here. The original card describes the anti-weaponization fund as "halted" and states that acting AG Todd Blanche said it "would not move forward." However, the source material shows Trump actively defending the fund as a "great idea" and refusing to rule out using it to compensate Capitol rioters who assaulted police.

These narratives are contradictory. The sources don't clearly establish that the fund was actually halted or that alternative pathways are being pursued—instead they show Trump continuing to support the fund's concept.

I cannot rewrite this card based on the provided sources because they don't substantiate the original premise. I'd need clarification on:
Whether the fund was officially halted
The current status of DOJ's involvement
Evidence of alternative pathways being explored

Could you provide source material that confirms the fund's cancellation and the pursuit of alternative compensation mechanisms?

cards.headline: Republican senator says Pulte unqualified for permanent intelligence role
cards.teaser: Senator James Lankford cited Bill Pulte's lack of national security experience.
cards.body:
Senator James Lankford of Oklahoma said Federal Housing Finance Agency Director Bill Pulte is not qualified to permanently serve as Director of National Intelligence. Lankford pointed to Pulte's lack of experience in national security as the key reason for his assessment.

Pulte currently heads the agency that oversees housing finance. Lankford made clear that while Pulte may be serving in the intelligence role temporarily, he lacks the background needed for the position on a long-term basis.
